To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the T‐shaped G3‐Fc structure is in agreement with SAXS data and the hydrodynamic properties determined experimentally.
the T‐shape of the G3‐IgG Fc protein is a consequence of the high affinity of the Fc domains to bind to each other.
the G3 domain is a T‐shape molecule that is anchored on the surface of the Fc domain.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and characterization of the recombinantly produced agrin G3‐Fc hybrid protein.
the structural analysis of a recombinant protein that is a potential tool to investigate new interactions of agrin.
the development and characterization of a new recombinant protein, which will be used in future to study the binding of agrin and its G3 domain to its ligands.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the recombinant G3‐Fc molecule has a T‐shape in solution, with an overall length of about 14 nm.
the G3 domain is not able to adopt a fully extended conformation and is forced to bend by the Fc domain.
the G3 domain is not able to adopt a conformation in the fusion protein that resembles its native state, and that the T‐shaped conformation is the most likely conformation of the G3‐Fcs protein.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the G3 domain is able to adopt a T‐shap structure, which is stabilized by the Fc domain.
our SAXS models are reliable.
we have produced a novel recombinant fusion molecule that can be used in the future to investigate binding partners of agrins.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the G3 domain can adopt an extended conformation and that the Fc scaffold is able to support the G3 domain in an extended conformation.
we have developed a novel tool to study the interactions of agrin and its domains with other proteins and molecules.
